Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:10:1.english: With regard to killing - The killing of the snake.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:10:2.hebrew: לא אמרינן - מאי בעי ידך כו', ואפילו כחצר המזיק דמיא, אינו פטור אלא נהרג. אלא לענין נזקין אמרינן מאי בעית ברשותי, כדתנן בפ"ק (דף ט:) חוץ מרשות המיוחדת למזיק; ומיבעיא לן פי פרה אי כחצר המזיק דמי או לא, עד דפשיטנא לה מכלב שנטל חררה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:10:2.english: We do not say - "What is your hand doing," etc.; and even if [it] is like the courtyard of the damager, he is not exempt, rather he is put to death. Rather, with regard to damages we say, "What are you doing in my domain?" — as we learned in the Mishnah in the first chapter (9b): "Except for a domain designated for the damager" — and [regarding] the mouth of a cow, it is a dilemma for us whether it is like the courtyard of the damager or not, until we resolve it from [the case of] a dog that took a cake.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:13:1.english: Bei Tarbu - [This is] the name of a family.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:15:1.english: Those that ascend - From Babylonia to the Land of Israel.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:15:2.hebrew: ודנחתין לתחתא - מארץ ישראל לבבל, הוו בקיאין בדין זה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:15:2.english: And those who descend below - [that is,] from the Land of Israel to Babylonia, be versed in this law.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:15:3.hebrew: עיזי דשוקא - דקצבי דקיימי לשחיטה, אלא דמשהו להו עד יומא דשוקא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:15:3.english: Goats of the market - [Goats] of butchers that stand [designated] for slaughter, except that they hold them until market day.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:15:4.english: We warn their owners - If they cause damage, even in the public domain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:15:5.english: Sit at the mesachta - [This is] the place where the butchers stand.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:15:6.hebrew: וקביל זוזך - אפילו ביומא דלאו דשוקא שחיט להו, הואיל ולשחיטה קיימן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:15:6.english: And take your money - Even on a day that is not a market day, he slaughters them, since they are meant for slaughter.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:16:1.hebrew: משיחזור בו שלשה ימים - שרואה שוורים ואינו נוגח, חוזר לתמותו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:16:1.english: From when it reverses its [behavior for] three days - [When] it sees oxen and does not gore, it returns to its innocuous status.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:16:2.english: Three times - And even on one day.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:17:1.hebrew: אתאן לנגיחה רביעית - שאם לא שמרו ונגח נגיחה רביעית, משלם מעלייה נ"ש, אבל אשלישית פלגא נזקא הוא דמשלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:17:1.english: We arrive at a fourth goring - For if he did not guard it and it gored a fourth time, he pays full damages from [his] superior [property], but for the third [goring], it is half damages that he pays.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:18:1.hebrew: ולא ישמרנו האידנא - בנגיחה שלישית, חייב עליה נזק שלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:18:1.english: "And he has not guarded it" now - On the third goring, he is liable for it [to pay] full damages.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:1:1.english: It is like the courtyard of the injured [party] - and we apply [the verse] "another's field" to it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:3:1.hebrew: ואי אמרת כו' - גמרא קמהדר, כלומר: אמאי מספקא לך? פשיטא דכחצר הניזק דמי, דאי כחצר המזיק דמי, א"כ שן דחייב רחמנא היכי משכחת לה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:3:1.english: And if you say, etc. - The Gemara is responding, that is to say: Why are you in doubt? It is obvious that it is like the courtyard of the injured party, for if it were like the courtyard of the damager, if so, how would you find [a case of] Tooth for which the Merciful One holds [one] liable?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:4:1.hebrew: נתחככה בכותל - דתולדה דשן היא, אבל שן ממש לא, דאמר ליה: פי פרתי רשותי היא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:4:1.english: Rubbed against a wall - For it is a derivative of Eating, whereas actual Eating [would] not [render him liable], for he says to him: "My cow's mouth is my domain."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:4:2.hebrew: וטנפה פירות - ע"י גלגול, כעין שעושין סוסים וחמורים, ובלעז וולט"ר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:4:2.english: And it soiled produce - By rolling, as horses and donkeys do, and in Old French, voltrer [to wallow].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:5:1.hebrew: והא בעינן עד תומו - דמכליא קרנא, דהא "ובער" זה השן מ"יבער הגלל עד תומו" נפקא לן בפ' קמא (דף ב:), והכא ליכא תומו, שעדיין האבנים והפירות בעין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:5:1.english: But we require “until it be all gone” - [Meaning] that it destroys the principal; for [the rule that] “and it consumes” refers to Tooth is derived for us from “[as] consumes the dung until it be all gone” in the first chapter (2b), and here there is no “until it be all gone,” since the stones and the produce are still intact.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:5:2.hebrew: דשף צלמי - כשנתחככה בכותל, מחקה צורה שעליו, דאיכא תומו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:5:2.english: That it erased images - When [the cow] rubbed against the wall, it erased a figure that was on it, so that there is [the condition of] "until it be all gone."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:5:3.hebrew: דפסעי פסועי - כשנתגלגלה על הפירות, תחבתן בטיט ואי אפשר ללקטן. לישנא אחרינא: דפסאי פסואי, כמו פסו אמונים (תהילים י״ב:ב׳), כלומר ששפכה משקה בגלגולה, דכליא ופסיא קרנא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:5:3.english: That trods [and presses] - When [the animal] rolled upon the produce, it pressed them into the mud, and it is impossible to gather them. Another version: defas'ai pasu'ai [meaning "ceased"], like "the faithful have vanished [pasu emunim]" (Psalms 12:2) — that is to say, it spilled a liquid by its rolling, so that the principal is consumed and vanishes.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:6:1.english: The one who incites is exempt - For indirect causation in damages is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:7:1.hebrew: דאפקיה לניביה - שהוציא שיניו וסרטו, דלא הכניס ידו לתוך פיו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:7:1.english: That [the dog] extended its canine teeth - That it stuck out its teeth and scratched him, such that [the victim] did not insert his hand into its mouth.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:8:1.hebrew: השיך בו את הנחש - שנטל את הנחש בידו, והגיע פיו ליד חבירו, עד שנכנסה לתוכו ונשכו ומת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:8:1.english: He caused the snake to bite him - That he took the snake in his hand and brought its mouth to his fellow's hand until [the hand] entered into it, and it bit him and he died.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:9:1.english: [It] stands between its fangs - And without the snake's intention, the venom comes out.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:9:2.hebrew: לפיכך מכיש בסייף - דהוה ליה כאילו הרגו בסייף, שהורג ממש הוא ולא גורם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:9:2.english: Therefore, the one who causes [the snake] to strike is [executed] by the sword - For it is as if he killed him with a sword, as he is an actual killer and not [merely] an indirect cause.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:9:3.hebrew: נחש בסקילה - כדין שור הורג אדם, דכתיב: "השור יסקל" (שמות כא):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 23b:9:3.english: [The] snake [is subject to] stoning - Like the law of an ox that kills a person, as it is written: "The ox shall be stoned" (Exodus 21).

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23b:13:1.hebrew: יכלי למימר לגדור מר גדירא בארעיה - היה נשמט אביי, שלא היה חפץ לילך לשם, דהתנן (לעיל בבא קמא דף יט:): "אכלה מתוך החנות משלמת כו'", ולא אמרינן היה לו לנעול חנותו; וכן "אכלה מצידי הרחבה". ולעיל נמי לא פריך דליפטר בעל הכלב מן החררה. ורב אלפס פסק כרב יוסף, וליתיה לדאביי, דדחויא בעלמא הוא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23b:13:1.english: "They can say: Let the Master put a fence up around his property" - Abaye was evading [going], as he did not want to go there, for we learned in the Mishnah (above, Bava Kamma 19b): "[If] it ate from inside the shop, she pays, etc.," and we do not say [that] he should have locked his shop; and similarly, "[if] it ate from the sides of the plaza." And above as well, [the Gemara] does not ask that the owner of the dog should be exempt [from paying] for the cake. And Rav Alfas ruled like Rav Yosef, and [the statement of] Abaye is not [accepted as halakhah], for it is merely a deflection.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23b:15:1.hebrew: הנהו עיזי דשוקא כו' - דוקא בהנהו דקיימי לשחיטה, ואע"ג שישלמו מה שהזיקו — לא בעי למיקם בהדייהו לדינא, וזימנין נמי דליכא סהדי. אבל עז לחלבה ורחל לגיזתה — יכול לומר: כשיזיק ישלם, כדאשכחן גבי עיזי דבי תרבו, דאמר ליה: זיל אצנעינהו, ולא אמר ליה: זיל שחטינהו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23b:15:1.english: "Those goats of the market, etc." - [This applies] specifically to those [goats] that stand for slaughter; and even though [the owners] will pay for what they damaged, [the injured parties] do not want to go to court with them, and sometimes too there are no witnesses. However, [regarding] a goat [kept] for its milk or a ewe [kept] for its shearing, [the owner] can say, "When it causes damage, [I] will pay," as we find regarding the goats of the Tarbu family, where [Rav Yosef] said to him, "Go, guard them," and did not say to him, "Go, slaughter them."

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23b:16:1.hebrew: איזהו מועד כו' - אומר ר"י, דהא דאמרינן בהבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף סד:), דסתם לן תנא דשור המועד כרשב"ג, דאמר בשלש זימנין הוי חזקה — לא משום דתיהוי פלוגתייהו בשור המועד, דמקראי דרשינן:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23b:16:1.english: Which [is] forewarned, etc. - Ri says that [regarding] that which we say in [the chapter] Haba Al Yevimto (Yevamot 64b), that the Tanna taught us anonymously [the law of] a forewarned ox in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who says that in three times a presumption is established — [this is] not because their dispute [applies] to a forewarned ox, for we expound [that] from verses:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23b:16:2.hebrew: שיהו התינוקות כו' - אף על גב דאדם אית ליה מזלא, מ"מ כיון שנעשה שפל כל כך שהתינוקות ממשמשין בו, ודאי חזר לקדמותו. ולא בא ר"מ למעט שלא תועיל חזרה שלשה ימים, אלא השמיענו דאפילו ביום אחד פעמים דאיכא חזרה, כגון ע"י תינוקות. וג' פעמים ביום אחד נראה דאין מועיל לדידיה לחזרה, אע"פ שמועיל להעדאה; דה"נ אשכחן לר"ש דבשלשה פעמים הוי מועד, ובחזרה בעי ג' ימים:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23b:16:2.english: "Where children [pet it], etc." - Even though a person has a mazal [protective fortune], nevertheless, since it has become so docile that children pet it, it has certainly reverted to its original [innocuous] state. And Rabbi Meir did not come to exclude [the three-day rule, i.e., to say] that a three-day reversion is not effective; rather, he teaches us that even on a single day there are times when reversion occurs, such as through children. And [refraining from goring] three times on one day — it appears that it is not effective according to him for reversion, even though it is effective for forewarning; for we find the same regarding Rabbi Shimon, that with three times it becomes forewarned, yet for reversion he requires three days.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23b:18:1.hebrew: ולא ישמרנו האידנא חייב - פי' בקונטרס בפי' ראשונה דלרבא בפעם ג' חייב נ"ש, צ"ל לפי' הא דקאמר לקמן דאתו ג' כיתי סהדי בחד יומא, דלמ"ד לייעודי תורא אייעד, ומשלמין בעלים נ"ש אע"פ שלא ידעו תחלה. ואינו נראה, ד"והועד בבעליו" כתיב, ואח"כ "אם לא ישמרנו" משלם נ"ש; וברייתא דלקמן קתני דאין השור נעשה מועד עד שיעידו בפני בעלים, וא"כ אפילו למ"ד לייעודי תורא צריך שידעו הבעלים תחלה, וכי אתו ג' כיתי סהדי בחד יומא והעידו בבעלים לא ישלמו בעלים נ"ש עד נגיחה ד'. ורש"י עצמו חזר בו, משום דבריש חזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף כח. ושם) קאמר סתמא דגמרא: "אי מה שור המועד עד נגיחה ד' לא מיחייב כו'", ופי' דמשמעות דורשין איכא בינייהו. והר"ר עזריאל פי' דאיכא בינייהו: דלאביי, דדריש "לא ישמרנו" לנגיחה ד', לא משלם נזק שלם עד יום ד', ד"לא ישמרנו" הוי יום ד' דומיא ד"תמול שלשום"; אבל לרבא, דלא כתיב נגיחה ד', אפילו נגח ד' בג' חייב. וקשה למאי דפי' דלא משלם ברביעית נ"ש אפי' למ"ד לייעודי תורא אא"כ העידו בבעלים בנגיחה ג', דאמרינן לקמן בפרק שור שנגח ארבעה וחמשה (בבא קמא דף מא. ושם): "וכי מאחר דמתם קטלינן ליה מועד היכי משכחת לה?" ומשני: "כגון שהוזמו זוממי זוממין", ופריך: "הניחא אי לייעודי תורא שפיר, אלא אי לייעודי גברא בעינן מצי אמר ליה לא הוה ידענא דתוראי נגחן". ולפי מה שפיר', אפילו אי לייעודי תורא נמי לא אתי שפיר! וי"ל דלכתחילה כשהוזמו השלשה כיתות לקחו הבעלים את השור, וכשבאו זוממי זוממין והעידו בבעליו בבית דין לא הספיקו לגמור את דינו עד שנגח נגיחה ד' בעוד שהיה בבית בעליו, וכמ"ד גומרין דינו של שור שלא בפניו; והו"מ למפרך: "הניחא למ"ד גומרין", אלא בלאו הכי פריך שפיר "הניחא" אחר. ור"ת מפרש שאין נאסר על ידי גמר דין כל זמן שהוא קיים, ועדיין שלו הוא עד לאחר סקילה או לאחר שחיטה; והשתא אתי שפיר אפי' נגמר דינו ואח"כ נגח. והא דקתני לקמן בברייתא: "נמצאת כת שלישית זוממת — כולן חייבין", אע"ג דעדיין לא חייב נזק שלם, מכל מקום כיון שמייעדין אותו וממילא מתחייב נזק שלם ברביעית, כשהוזמו צריכין לשלם כפי מה שתעלה נגיחה ד' כשיגח. אע"ג דבפרק הנחנקין (סנהדרין דף פו:) אמר: "עידי גניבה בנפש שהוזמו ועידי גניבה ראשונה של בן סורר אין נהרגין", התם לאו משום דיכול להיות שלא יבאו לידי חיוב פטרינן להו, אלא התם משום דמצו למימר: "להלקותו באנו", ועידי גניבה בנפש שהוזמו לוקין, כדפירש התם בקונטרס. אבל הכא ע"כ לא באו כי אם לייעדו ולחייבו נזק שלם כשיגח נגיחה ד', כדמסיק ואזיל, דלא מצו למימר: "לחיובי פלגא נזקא קאתינן". א"כ אין חייבין אלו הכיתות אלא במה שעשאו מועד, ואומדין כמה נפחת שורו מדמיו, ולא צריכא השתא לנגיחה רביעית כלל:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23b:18:1.english: "And [its owner] has not secured it" now, he is liable - Rashi explained in his first commentary that according to Rava, on the third time he is liable for full damages. According to his explanation, one must say [regarding] that which [the Gemara] states below — where three sets of witnesses come on one day — that according to the one who says [the three days are] to forewarn the ox, it becomes forewarned, and the owners pay full damages even though they did not know beforehand. But this does not seem [correct], for it is written, "and warning has been given to its owner" (Exodus 21:29), and afterward, [if] "he has not secured it," he pays full damages; and the Baraita below teaches that an ox does not become a mu'ad until they testify in the presence of the owners. And if so, even according to the one who says [the requirement is] to forewarn the ox, it is necessary that the owners know beforehand; and when three sets of witnesses come on one day and testify before the owners, the owners do not pay full damages until the fourth goring. And Rashi himself retracted [his first explanation], because at the beginning of [the chapter] Chezkat HaBatim (Bava Batra 28a, and there [in the parallel]), the anonymous Gemara states: "Just as a forewarned ox is not liable [for full damages] until the fourth goring, etc.," and he [Rashi, in his revised commentary] explained that the difference between them [Abaye and Rava] is [merely] how they expound the wording [of the verse]. And Rabbeinu Azriel explained that the difference between them is: according to Abaye, who expounds "he has not secured it" as referring to the fourth goring, he does not pay full damages until the fourth day, for "he has not secured it" is the fourth day, similar to "yesterday [and] the day before yesterday"; whereas according to Rava, for whom the fourth goring is not written [in the verse], even if it gored four [times] in three [days], he is liable [for full damages]. And it is difficult according to what [we] explained — that he does not pay full damages on the fourth [goring] even according to the one who says [it is] to forewarn the ox unless they testified before the owners at the third goring — for we say below in the chapter Shor SheNagach Arba'ah VaChamishah (Bava Kamma 41a, and there): "Since we put it to death from [the time it was a] tam, how can you find a mu'ad?" And [the Gemara] answers: "For example, where the zomemei zomemin [witnesses who refuted the scheming witnesses] were themselves proven zomemin," and [the Gemara] objects: "This works well if [the three days are] to forewarn the ox — fine; but if we require forewarning the owner, he can say to him: I did not know that my ox was a gorer." Now, according to what we explained, even if [it is] to forewarn the ox, it also does not work well! And one can answer that initially, when the three sets [of witnesses] were proven zomemin, the owners took the ox [back], and when the zomemei zomemin came and testified against its owner in court, they did not manage to conclude its verdict before it gored a fourth goring while it was still in its owner's house — and [this accords] with the one who says that they conclude the verdict of an ox even in its absence. And [the Gemara] could have objected: "This works well according to the one who says they conclude [its verdict in its absence]," but even without that, it objects well [with] another "This works well" [question]. And Rabbeinu Tam explains that it does not become forbidden [for benefit] through the conclusion of the verdict as long as it is alive, and it is still his until after stoning or after slaughter; and now it works well even if its verdict was concluded and afterward it gored. And [as for] that which is taught below in the Baraita: "If the third set is found to be zomemin, all of them are liable" — even though [the owner] is not yet liable for full damages, nevertheless, since they are rendering it a mu'ad and consequently he will become liable for full damages on the fourth [goring], when they are proven zomemin they must pay according to what the fourth goring will amount to when it gores. Even though in the chapter HaNechnakin (Sanhedrin 86b) it states: "Witnesses to the kidnapping of a person who were proven zomemin, and witnesses to the first stealing of a stubborn and rebellious son, are not executed" — there, it is not because it is possible that they would not come to liability [for execution] that we exempt them; rather, there it is because they can say: "We came [only] to have him flogged," and witnesses to kidnapping who were proven zomemin are flogged, as Rashi explained there. But here, perforce they came only to render it a mu'ad and to make him liable for full damages when it gores a fourth goring, as [the Gemara] goes on to conclude, for they cannot say: "We came to make him liable for half-damages." If so, these sets [of witnesses] are liable only for that by which they made it a mu'ad, and they assess how much his ox's value decreased, and now [this] does not depend on a fourth goring at all.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23b:6:1.hebrew: תא שמע שיסה בו את הכלב - ותימה, דאמאי לא משני "לענין קטלא לא אמרינן", כדאמרינן בסמוך? דהך משנה היא רישא ד"השיך בו את הנחש" דמייתי בתר הכי בפ' אלו הן הנשרפין (סנהדרין דף עו: ושם). ושמא משמע ליה רישא בין לענין מיתה בין לענין נזקין, ולקמן נמי מייתי לה גבי בעיא משסה כלבו של חבירו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23b:6:1.english: Come and hear: If he incited a dog against him - And it is astonishing: why does [the Gemara] not answer, "With regard to capital punishment we do not say [this]," as we say shortly [below]? For this Mishnah is the first clause of "If one caused a snake to bite him," which [the Gemara] cites right after this, in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Hen HaNisrafin (Sanhedrin 76b and there [in our Gemara]). And perhaps the first clause implies to it both with regard to death and with regard to damages, and later on as well, [the Gemara] cites it regarding the dilemma of one who incites another's dog:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23b:7:1.hebrew: דאפקיה לניביה וסרטיה - הו"מ לשנויי', כגון שלא הכניס יד חבירו, אלא הכלב עצמו לקחה כששיסהו; אלא דמשני לפי מה שסבור דמיירי כשהושיט לו ידו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 23b:7:1.english: That [the dog] extended its canine tooth and scratched him - [The Gemara] could have answered [that it is] a case where his fellow did not insert [his] hand, rather the dog itself took it when [the inciter] incited it; however, it answers according to what [the questioner] assumed — that [the Mishnah] is dealing with [a case] where he extended his hand to it.
